svg.title: Thread binding lifecycle
svg.desc: Writers create task and run bindings in ThreadBindingStore, which persists them to thread-bindings.json. ThreadBindingLifecycleManager and explicit unbind remove task bindings, the run subscriber removes its run binding, ThreadBindingRouter reads task bindings on every inbound message, and reconcile drops bindings of terminal or unknown targets at startup.

g.text: Hover a box for its trigger, source file or failure mode; its connections light up. Click it to open its section.
Inside a rendered document this image is static. Click it to open the interactive SVG.

svg.text: A task binding routes a thread to a task session; a run binding only holds a run's thread, so the idle sweep skips it.

g.text: run notification · task/workflow_run_notification_subscriber.dart; writes ThreadBinding.run for a run on chat_notifications
Not written for a run posted into its origin thread. The store exists when workflow.chat_notifications is configured even with thread_binding off.
task notification · task/task_notification_subscriber.dart; the flag on, a channel-originated task first post writes the binding
The binding carries the task origin's session key. Only a channel that declares ThreadedNotifications can hold one.
explicit bind (admin) · reserved_command_handler.dart, mcp/task_tools.dart, api/task_routes.dart; one thread key via the capability
Each refuses a terminal or unknown task, a thread bound to another task, and a thread held by a run binding.
holds the thread a run posts into
routes nothing: router lookups skip it
ThreadBinding.run · targetId is the run ID, no sessionKey; exempt from the sweep: a run can wait at an approval longer than the timeout
Only the run subscriber deletes it (deleteByTarget in _closeRun, after the terminal post and any unresolved-approval edit) or startup reconcile.
routes the thread to a task session
lastActivity: set on every routed message
removed by: terminal task, idle sweep,
ThreadBinding.task · immutable record; in-memory map persisted with atomic temp-file-and-rename writes
Lookups are synchronous, only writes touch disk. load() keeps every well-formed row: it runs before channels register.
run finished · deleteByTarget(ThreadBindingKind.run, runId) once the run ends, after the terminal post and any unresolved-approval edit
A run that is cancelled by an approval timeout is edited to "No longer pending" first.
terminal task · deleteByTaskId when the task reaches accepted, rejected, cancelled or failed; cleanup operations are serialized
A persistence failure is logged and never blocks later cleanup; dispose() cancels new work and drains pending writes.
idle sweep · features.thread_binding.idle_timeout_minutes, default 60, 1 to 1440; removeExpiredBindings skips run bindings
Removal can lag the timeout by up to one sweep interval.
explicit unbind · /unbind, task_unbind and DELETE /api/tasks/<id>/bindings/... remove one task binding on request
A thread held by a run binding answers a conflict naming the run; no writer can remove it.
ChannelManager · asks ThreadBindingRouter for a binding on every inbound message, before the pause check
The thread comes from the owning channel's ThreadedNotifications.extractThread, so reads and writes agree on the key.
ThreadBindingRouter · thread_binding_router.dart; returns a binding only if it is a task binding, so a run binding never answers
The lastActivity write is awaited before the message is enqueued on binding.sessionKey.
Passes non-terminal task and run IDs to ThreadBindingStore.reconcile; load() cannot tell a stale row from one whose channel is starting.
